events.title: The microphones are waiting
events.speaker: Postgame reporter
events.win: “That performance is going to be part of the conversation after this win. What should people understand about how it happened—and what comes next?”
events.loss: “Your individual performance stood out, but the team did not win. How do you talk about your own night without losing sight of the result?”
events.tie: “Your individual performance stood out in a tied game. What do you take from it, and what does the team still need to finish?”

choices.label: Share the credit
choices.description: Talk about the teammates and preparation behind your performance.
choices.outcome: You put other names into the interview. The locker room appreciates being part of the story.

choices.label: Set a higher standard
choices.description: Say this is the level you intend to keep chasing.
choices.outcome: Your ambition becomes the headline. The staff hears confidence, and a standard it will expect you to work toward.

events.title: A knock on the office door
events.speaker: Position coach
events.win: “That was a big contribution to a win. I want to know what we can repeat when the opponent takes away your first answer. How do you want to use the next review?”
events.loss: “Your production deserves recognition. The result also tells us that one player’s line cannot answer every question. What should our next review focus on?”
events.tie: “There is plenty to build on in your performance, but the game still ended level. What do you want to learn from the next review?”

choices.label: Find the repeatable decisions
choices.description: Review the reads and preparation behind the performance.
choices.outcome: You and the coach turn the big game into specific preparation notes. The staff trusts your approach a little more.

choices.label: Ask to compete for more responsibility
choices.description: Use the performance to make a case, without assuming a promotion.
choices.outcome: The coach agrees to keep evaluating your case. No real-game rotation or depth-chart change has been promised.

events.title: One more conversation in the locker room
events.speaker: Veteran teammate
events.win: “People will remember your numbers from this win. I want to know what you saw out there. Can we work through it together?”
events.loss: “You had a big game, and the loss still hurts. We can recognize what you did without pretending the job is done. How do we build from here?”
events.tie: “You had a big game, even if neither team finished ahead. What can the rest of us learn from what you saw?”

choices.label: Bring everyone into the review
choices.description: Share what worked and ask what teammates saw.
choices.outcome: Your teammates leave with a clearer picture of your decisions. The big game becomes something the group can learn from.

choices.label: Protect your individual routine
choices.description: Explain the preparation you want to keep doing on your own.
choices.outcome: The veteran respects the work, but notices the distance. You keep ownership of your routine and a more independent reputation.
